dev_notes: src/commands/write.mjs cmdChange, with cmdUpdate as the deprecated alias that turns each old bullet into a `combined` event. Events are appended to the feature's `events` with version, kind, what, why, why_from and date; a change with no history entry at the open release creates one, copying the previous description when none is given. Category, sub-section, size and dev_notes alone are filing and record nothing; a `paths` field is dropped with a note. A why_from of commit or unknown is listed by unknownReasons() in src/compose.mjs.

history.name: Recording a change to a feature
history.description: The command ledger update replaces a feature's description with its full current-state text, and takes a list of change bullets alongside it. Each bullet says what the feature was before and why it moved, which is the part a reader cannot get from the description. A feature that existed before this release cannot be updated without one, so an edition never carries a changed entry with no reason attached.

The command ledger update replaces a feature's description with its full current-state text, and takes a list of change bullets alongside it. Each bullet says what the feature was in the last edition and why it moved, which is the part a reader cannot get from the description. A feature that existed before this release cannot be updated without one, so an edition never carries a changed entry with no reason attached. A feature that is new in this release takes no change bullets, because the client has never seen an earlier version of it. When a feature changes a second time in one release, the command reminds you that its bullets have to be true of the last edition, not of the state your previous update left.

The command ledger change records what moved in a feature and why, with the new description and how to see it when those moved too. A reason nobody can give is kept as a question rather than guessed, and moving an entry's size or area records nothing.
history.how_to_see: Run ledger change on an entry with --what and --why-unknown, then run ledger on its own: the change is listed under the reasons nobody has vouched for.

events.what: A change is recorded as two facts, what moved and why, instead of as a bullet written for the client when the change landed. The note the edition prints is composed later, for the whole release.
events.why: A bullet written mid-release described the state just before that update, which the client often never saw, and a review had to repair the release before every cut. A note composed once, from the last edition and the current one, can't describe a state the client never had.

events.what: A change can also say how to see the entry: the instructions a client follows to check it.
events.why: So a client can check each claim for themselves.
